articles.title: Will Republicans learn from this defeat?
articles.summary: A healthy Republican Party would respond to this historic midterm-election repudiation of President Donald Trump with contrition and honest introspection. Its leaders would plot a fresh path forward and shed the elements of a White House agenda that drove American voters to hand control of the House of Representatives and US Senate to a Democratic Party they don’t even approve of all that much.Reduced to a rump in Congress and its governing coalition gutted to the bone — just in time for 2028 — that Republican Party would assemble a more durable confederation of voters that doesn’t rise and fall on the whims of a narcissistic albeit once-in-a-generation political talent.But Republicans and their exalted leader aren’t the picture of political health.Those within the party most likely to confront reality and take on the difficult work of rebuilding the GOP were cut down in ruby-red House districts, Senate seats and governors’ mansions that have simply not elected Democrats. The only Republicans left standing were insulated — by gerrymandered districts, their constituents’ stubborn support for Trump or a combination of the two. The party’s short-sighted motivation will be to follow the president’s defiant lead and resist the new Democratic majorities’ attempts to neuter the commander-in-chief.And so the party’s future, immediate and otherwise, is in Trump’s hands, and most elected officials would still take their cues from the White House.As the shocking returns flowed in showing defeats in Senate contests in Iowa, Kansas, Ohio, South Carolina and Texas (Texas!), some veteran party insiders I spoke with disagreed with my assessment and argued that battered congressional Republicans would be chastened, distance themselves from Trump and finally end blind support for his agenda on Capitol Hill. Some Republican operatives even speculated that Vice President JD Vance would be forced to abandon any plans he might have to seek the White House, to say nothing of aspiring Cabinet members.I’m not a gambler. But if I were, I wouldn’t risk a nickel on that bet. The siren song of the president’s loyal, Make American Great Again (MAGA) populist base will be hard for the party’s 2028 contenders to resist — and that’s if a major effort materializes to wean the party off of Trump.This isn’t the first time the president has led his party into a ditch, only to recover like Lazarus because he refused to concede failure. That kind of obstinance inspires grassroots conservatives who see a fighter rather than a shirker. “I wasn’t on the ballot and if I was, we would have won IN A LANDSLIDE!” Trump said in a Truth Social post on election night. Meanwhile, GOP strategists told me with a high degree of confidence that Democrats will overplay their hand — just like Republicans did — causing voters to turn back to Trump and the GOP just in time for a presidential campaign now unexpectedly ripe with opportunity.The claim that Democrats will overreach and offer Republicans a chance to revive their political standing is not unreasonable; the US has seen both political parties misinterpret an election backlash. The Democrats did so following back-to-back blue waves in 2006 and 2008. Two years later in 2010, a red wave gained the GOP 63 House districts and seven Senate seats during President Barack Obama’s first midterm election. The Republicans committed the same faux pas during Trump’s first presidency, which fueled a blue wave-flip of 41 House districts in the 2018 midterm election.No doubt, if Democrats dive head first into impeaching Trump and legislate on culture-war issues after the new Congress is seated in January, voters will sour on them rather quickly. But I wonder if Republicans have digested the breadth of the destruction the 45th and 47th president left in his wake this week — an apocalyptic political disaster that, as polling analyst Sean Trende points out, hasn’t been seen since 1974, in the aftermath of the Watergate scandal that left the GOP on life support.Republicans didn’t just lose a Senate seat in Kansas for the first time in nearly a century. The Democrats were possibly poised to win a Senate seat in Mississippi for the first time since 1982. The GOP lost states, districts and other offices that Trump and his GOP predecessors have been carrying by double digits going back years, if not decades. That outcome demands a wholesale reevaluation of American politics and the blue-state, red-state paradigm the US has lived under for a quarter century.Trump doesn’t seem much interested in doing so. And if past is prologue, that means Republicans won’t be either. They might need to lose some more, first.

articles.title: Decoding a Rep firebrand's high-decibel fall
articles.summary: Vivek Ramaswamy's meteoric rise was built on the promise that an outsider equipped with sharp rhetoric, business credentials and unwavering loyalty to Donald Trump could reshape the fortunes of the Republican Party. His defeat in Ohio at the US midterms today could be proof that national-level visibility, proximity to the president and political acumen may not be enough to convert big political fame into a poll success story.Democrat Amy Acton defeated the Trump-backed Ramaswamy in the Ohio governor's race, ending Republican control of the state governor office and delivering Democrats their first victory in the contest in 20 years.Also read | US has no immediate plan to strike Iran, Trump tells FTJust ahead of the vote, Ramaswamy drew public attention in stunning fashion by bringing out a highly controversial ad based on an episode from Acton's personal life. The ad eventually went on to divide opinions like few other ads in recent memory.As Ramaswamy's camapaign for the high-profile seat got progressively heated up, Trump and Vice-President JD Vance repeatedly travelled to Ohio to campaign for him.The win for Acton, who also became the first woman elected governor of Ohio, came despite more than $100 million being spent against her on the strength of substantial financial backing from Ramaswamy's allies.Decoding a high-profile lossRamaswamy's defeat is significant because he was more than an ordinary Republican gubernatorial candidate. The biotech entrepreneur had emerged as one of the most recognisable faces of the party's new generation, using television debates, social media and provocative political arguments to build a national following.His 2021 bestseller Woke, Inc. helped establish his credentials as an anti-woke conservative. During the 2024 Republican presidential primaries, his combative debate performances and uncompromising positions attracted considerable attention, even though he eventually finished fourth in the Iowa caucuses before withdrawing and endorsing Trump.Also read | 'We would have won a landslide': Trump claims Republicans would have won big if on ballotHis political ascent also earned him a brief role alongside Elon Musk in the Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE).His ability to articulate the MAGA movement's positions with unusual energy made him an influential political communicator. He also helped broaden the Republican Party's appeal by demonstrating that its conservative nationalist message could be championed by an Indian-American Hindu.His defeat is now raising questions about whether national fame can translate into support at the state level.The limits of MAGAFor Trump, the result could be a marked setback. Ramaswamy had the president's backing, substantial campaign resources and support from prominent Republicans. These big advantages, however, failed to overcome voter concerns about affordability, rising living costs and fuel prices.Acton, on the other hands, made these issues central to her campaign, which likely played a huge role in giving her the win.Ramaswamy's loss also might go on to show that Trump's political influence has limits, particularly when voters are focused on other important issues.The ad featuring Acton's estranged mother may have added a major layer of complication to Ramaswamy's campaign. The advertisement divided opinions sharply and drew fierce criticism from both Republicans and Democrats.Trump publicly defended Ramaswamy's ad and his decision to run it. It probably turned out to be one of the factors that backfired on their high-decibel campaign, with voters taking strong issue with a move made in bad taste.No country for loud menFor Republicans, Ohio may have just offered a warning -- that political savvy, money & fundraising muscle and sleek rhetoric don't guarantee a win.For Ramaswamy, this defeat does not diminish him or erode his ability to shape conservative debates. What it actually does is, it exposes the gap between being a MAGA bigshot and turning that into a poll win.Some analysts also said this loss might also toughen things for new Republican faces hoping to inherit Trump's legacy. Ramaswamy had positioned himself as a flagbearer of that generation. His fall may have just suggested that the party's future will depend not just on sharp rhetoric and money power, but also on how it addresses actual socio-economic issues.

articles.title: Explained: Why Sebi wants mutual fund investors to switch to direct plans
articles.summary: Sebi has directed mutual fund houses to make direct plans the default option on their digital platforms from 1st November. A look at the reason behind the regulator’s action.WHAT ARE DIRECT AND REGULAR PLANS IN MUTUAL FUNDS?Direct and regular plans are two ways of investing in a mutual fund scheme. In a direct plan, investors put money in a scheme without involving a distributor, broker or agent. Since no commission is paid, the scheme’s expense ratio or fee is lower.A regular plan is bought through a distributor, broker or adviser. The mutual fund pays a commission to the intermediary, and this cost is recovered from the investor through the scheme’s expense ratio. As a result, the expense ratio is higher than that of direct plans.According to the latest AMFI data, the total expense ratio (TER) of regular plans ranges from 0.36% to 4.3%, compared with 0% to 2.7% for direct plans.WHAT HAS SEBI CHANGED AND WHY?From November 1, Sebi has asked mutual fund houses to make direct plans the default option on their websites and mobile apps. So, if an investor visits a fund house’s app to invest in an equity scheme, the direct plan will now be pre-selected or displayed as the primary option. Investors can still choose regular plans if they want distributor assistance.Read more: Sebi levies Rs 40 lakh penalty on four entities in Axis MF front-running caseBUT WHAT’S WRONG WITH REGULAR PLANS?There is nothing wrong per se with regular plans. In fact, it may be suitable for investors seeking professional guidance or those new to mutual funds. After all, distributors handle the client portfolios and do periodic reviews of the holdings.But, critics point out that in addition to the higher costs, regular plans could result in conflict of interest. Since distributors are paid commissions by fund houses, this would push some intermediaries to recommend schemes that offer higher commissions rather than those best suited for client needs. They claim investors would be better off availing the services of fee-based financial advisers, who charge investors directly for their advice.HOW MUCH MONEY CAN INVESTORS SAVE THROUGH LOWER EXPENSE RATIOS?While the difference in the total expense ratio may appear small, it can significantly impact returns over long investment horizons.For instance, an investor putting Rs 20,000 a month into an equity mutual fund for 15 years, assuming annual returns of 12%, could accumulate around Rs 94.4 lakh in a direct plan with a 0.7% expense ratio. In comparison, the corpus would be about Rs 86 lakh in a regular plan with a 1.7% expense ratio.The difference arises because lower expenses leave more money invested, allowing returns to compound over time.Read more: Quant Mutual Fund reduces exposure to frontline IT stocks as part of profit-booking exerciseWHO SHOULD CONSIDER DIRECT PLANS?Direct plans are suitable for investors who can research funds, monitor their portfolios and make investment decisions independently or with the help of fee-based advisors.If you understand concepts such as asset allocation, risk management and portfolio rebalancing, and can stay invested through market cycles, a direct plan may be a good option.

'Tesla misled South Korean customers'
articles.summary: Tesla has misled tens of thousands of South Korean customers by marketing driver-assistance software that the company knows cannot be legally used in most of its vehicles in the country, according to a complaint an advocacy group plans to file with a consumer protection agency on Thursday.Tesla has marketed Full Self-Driving (Supervised) software to prospective buyers in South Korea for years, often collecting lump-sum payments of 9.043 million won ($6,726).FSD can be used on about 20% of Tesla vehicles registered in South Korea - those manufactured in the US, Tesla Korea country manager Seo Young-deuk said in parliamentary testimony last month. Those cars meet US vehicle-safety standards that South Korea recognizes as part of a free trade agreement, according to the forthcoming complaint to the Korea Fair Trade Commission (KFTC), seen by Reuters.The complaint to the regulator, which also handles antitrust, has not been previously reported.Most Tesla vehicles in South Korea, however, are manufactured in China, where no such agreement exists. Tesla only recently started the process for obtaining FSD certification for China-made vehicles, despite charging customers for the software for more than three years.SOUTH KOREAN TRADE COMMISSION INVESTIGATINGIt is unclear how many South Korean customers purchased FSD subscriptions on ineligible vehicles, but Tesla has sold more than 170,000 Shanghai-produced vehicles in South Korea since 2023, according to Tesla data sent to South Korea's National Assembly."Tesla generated substantial revenue by selling an expensive driver-assistance system to mass-market buyers who cannot use it for even a single day," said Choi Young-suk, who leads automotive issues at the advocacy group Citizens United for Consumer Sovereignty.Tesla did not respond to requests for comment. A KFTC official said the agency launched a probe earlier this year into Tesla's advertising of its FSD system and has received written responses from the company, but declined to provide further details.Tesla continued to market FSD as sales of ineligible China-manufactured Teslas surged in South Korea in recent years. Sales of FSD-incompatible Teslas made in China grew more than fivefold in South Korea from 2023 through last year, when 99% of new Teslas sold in South Korea could not legally use FSD, according to data Tesla submitted to the National Assembly.Despite years of promises from CEO Elon Musk that all Teslas would soon become fully driverless vehicles, FSD is not autonomous and requires active human supervision.Tesla has sought to expand FSD's reach beyond North America, particularly in Europe, where the company has waged a pressure campaign against European regulators.TESLA SALES SURGE IN SOUTH KOREATesla surpassed BMW this year as South Korea's top imported-car brand, according to South Korean import data.Tesla sold FSD for one-time payments for years, before shifting to a monthly subscription of 150,000 won ($112) in August.The complaint alleges that Tesla promoted FSD last year as "coming soon" and posted a demonstration video filmed in South Korea without clearly disclosing that the technology could only be used in a small fraction of Teslas being sold.Tesla knew those limitations but continued to market the software to all customers, the complaint said.Tesla Korea manager Seo testified during an October 8 parliamentary hearing that the company had not formally requested FSD testing from the transport ministry. Two weeks later, Tesla applied for certification.The ministry said FSD does not comply with local safety rules, including requirements for drivers to keep their hands on the wheel, according to a statement it sent to a lawmaker, reviewed by Reuters. The transport ministry could not be reached for comment.The consumer group accused Tesla Korea of deceptive marketing and asked the KFTC to issue a temporary cease-and-desist order on marketing FSD for ineligible vehicles, impose administrative fines and refer the case to state investigators.

We will decide the future course of action in our core committee meeting post Diwali on November 10 on the way to intensify struggle," United Forum of IDBI Officers and Employees convener Devidas Tuljapurkar said.Read more - Get ready to pay double for parking in Delhi: MCD plans to hike charges at 400 parking lots under GRAP-II; what two-wheeler and car owners need to knowHe added that the union would approach the United Forum of Bank Unions (UFBU) to seek wider support, including the possibility of a nationwide bank strike.IDBI Bank employees oppose proposed stake sale to FairfaxThe union has raised concerns about the valuation of the lender and the possibility of its assets and business capabilities being undervalued in the transaction."We are seriously concerned that the transaction may undervalue IDBI’s properties, institutional capabilities, customer relationships, future earnings and strategic importance," Tuljapurkar said.Read more - Rahul Gandhi vs Narendra Modi debate: RaGa asks public if they want open face-off; urges Nitin Gadkari, Yogi Adityanath & other BJP leaders to convince PMHe also called on the government to make the valuation process more transparent.
